units.title: 高级阅读：候补划手在岸边的一天

materials.title: The Spare Seat
materials.text:
The message arrived while I was packing my bag for the rowing trial. One of the regular crew had recovered sooner than expected, so I would be travelling as a reserve. I wrote back that I understood, then removed the spare racing shirt from my bag and put it back into the drawer. My sister noticed. “You might still need it,” she said. I told her that I was only trying to travel lightly.

At the river, the coach greeted me warmly and asked whether I would help carry the equipment. I agreed, though I could not prevent myself from counting the jobs I had done before anybody mentioned the possibility of my rowing. The regular crew discussed the current and the turn near the final marker. I knew those details too. I had practised the same course all week. Standing beside the boat, I felt that knowing the water was suddenly a private skill with no public use.

The first crew went out. A strong breeze had begun to press across the river, and their starting position drifted while they waited for a signal. From the bank, I could see one end moving faster than the other. I called to the coach, who walked closer to the water and repeated the warning. The crew corrected its position. Nobody turned towards me. I was annoyed by this until I noticed that none of them could safely spare the attention to look back.

After the first run, the coach asked what I had seen. I began with the uneven drift, then described the moment when the boat's line changed near the marker. He listened and asked me to watch for the same feature on the next run. This was more exacting than the general encouragement I had expected to offer from the bank. I had to distinguish something happening in the boat from something caused by my own changing viewpoint as I walked beside it.

During the break, the regular rower sat next to me. He asked if I was disappointed. I said that I had wanted the seat. He nodded without offering the comforting claim that being a reserve was just as satisfying. Then he asked to borrow my notes about the final turn. We talked about the part of the course that had troubled both of us. For the first time that morning, I stopped measuring our conversation against the place I had not been given.

I did not row that day. On the journey home, my sister asked whether the trip had been worth it. I said yes, but not because I had discovered that I never wanted to race. I wanted the seat as much as before. What had changed was the idea that wanting one role made every other contribution a consolation prize. When I unpacked, I went to the drawer for the racing shirt. I put it into the bag for the following week's practice, together with the notes I had made from the riverbank.

questions.prompt: What is implied by the narrator’s explanation about “travelling lightly”?
options: It partly conceals disappointment about not expecting to race.
It refers to a new rule limiting the crew’s luggage.
It shows that the narrator has permanently given up rowing.
It means that the coach had requested an empty bag.
questions.explanation: A正确：收到候补通知后拿出赛衣，又用轻装掩饰，结尾仍想争取座位。B没有行李规则；C下一周仍练并仍想参赛；D教练没要求空包。

questions.prompt: Why does the narrator revise the reaction to the crew’s failure to look back?
options: The crew later apologises for refusing assistance.
The narrator realises that looking back would distract them from handling the boat.
The warning turns out to concern a different boat.
The coach explains that nobody can hear from the bank.
questions.explanation: B正确：他看到队员无法安全分神回头，因而改看无人回望的反应。A没有道歉情节；C警告针对本队；D教练复述警告，非宣布听不到。

questions.prompt: What made the coach’s request demanding?
options: It required the narrator to draw the whole river from memory.
It required a prediction of the exact final race result.
It involved separating boat movement from changes in the observer’s viewpoint.
It prevented the narrator from taking any notes.
questions.explanation: C正确：移动观察时要区分船自身变化与视角变化，文中明确more exacting。A非凭记忆画全河；B没有预测终局；D他保留岸边笔记。

questions.prompt: How does the regular rower respond to the narrator’s disappointment?
options: By denying that the narrator wanted the place.
By promising to leave the crew immediately.
By insisting that reserve duty is equally satisfying.
By acknowledging it and discussing a shared practical difficulty.
questions.explanation: D正确：队员承认他想要座位，不说候补同样满足，继而讨论共同困扰的转弯。A他未否认感受；B无退队承诺；C作者明确未获这种安慰说法。

questions.prompt: Which idea changes by the end of the account?
options: Only the desired role can make a contribution worthwhile.
The narrator has no wish to compete again.
Watching from the bank requires no rowing knowledge.
The recovered rower was unfit to return.
questions.explanation: A正确：结尾说想要一个角色不等于其他贡献都只是安慰奖。B仍同样想赛位；C需要已有水情知识与准确观察；D康复队员正常归队，没有不适合的判断。

questions.prompt: What does putting the shirt and notes into the same bag suggest?
options: The narrator intends to replace practice with note-taking.
The narrator now carries both ambition and what was learned in the reserve role.
The notes will be discarded as soon as a seat is available.
The shirt has become useless to the narrator.
questions.explanation: B正确：赛衣代表仍存参赛愿望，岸边笔记代表候补角色获得的认识，两者并存。A没有替代划行练习；C没有弃笔记计划；D下周练习仍需赛衣。

units.title: 高级填空：桌游的第一步为何最难

materials.title: Before the First Move
materials.text:
For someone learning an unfamiliar board game, the hardest moment may come before the first move. The written rules can seem complete, yet a beginner may have no idea ____1____ to begin. Every term refers to another term, and the purpose of a rule may become clear only after it has been used.

One club dealt with this by separating a demonstration from a competitive game. An experienced player set out a few pieces and explained one choice at a time. The aim was not to reveal the best possible strategy, ____2____ alone to guarantee a win. It was to give newcomers enough experience to ask useful questions.

The demonstrator sometimes made a deliberately poor move. Far ____3____ hiding the mistake, she explained what it made possible for the other player. A rule that had looked arbitrary on paper then had an effect that everyone could see.

This approach did not mean that the rulebook could be put ____4____ permanently. When an unusual situation arose, players still needed to consult its exact wording. Nor did it mean that the demonstrator should decide every move on a beginner's ____5____. At some point, a new player had to choose and see what followed.

The club asked volunteers to leave time for that choice, no matter ____6____ obvious it seemed to them. Silence was not necessarily a sign that the explanation had failed. It might be the moment ____7____ a player was trying to connect a rule with a plan. The best help sometimes consisted ____8____ waiting long enough for that connection to be made.

questions.prompt: Gap 1: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: have no idea where/how to begin均是标准起步表达；what不能直接接to begin表达相同含义。

questions.prompt: Gap 2: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: let alone为更不用说的固定短语。

questions.prompt: Gap 3: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: Far from doing表示非但不……，此处不隐藏错误而解释结果。

questions.prompt: Gap 4: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: put aside/away/down the rulebook都可表示把书放在一旁不再查阅，本句否定永久如此；put off不能在此自然表示放下书本。

questions.prompt: Gap 5: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: on someone's behalf固定短语，表示替新手决定。

questions.prompt: Gap 6: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: no matter how+形容词obvious，不能用what修饰形容词。

questions.prompt: Gap 7: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: the moment when/that后接完整小句，两者可表示尝试联系规则和计划的时刻；which不能在该完整从句作所需时间状语。

questions.prompt: Gap 8: Write one word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: consist in waiting强调帮助的本质，consist of waiting强调组成内容，在此两种常见构式均合理。

units.title: 高级词形：考古现场的参观步道

materials.title: Making a Site Readable
materials.text:
An ____1____ (ARCHAEOLOGY) team preparing a site for visitors had to consider more than the objects already uncovered. The exposed surfaces were vulnerable to ____2____ (ERODE), particularly after heavy rain. Paths and shelters therefore formed part of the project from the beginning.

The team wanted the site to be ____3____ (ACCESS) without suggesting that every area could be opened at once. A narrow walkway allowed small groups to see one part of the excavation while work continued elsewhere. The route changed ____4____ (STEADY) as the ground conditions altered, and staff explained those changes at the entrance.

Beside the path, a display offered a ____5____ (COMPARE) between a newly exposed surface and a record made several seasons earlier. The purpose was not to make the earlier stage look unfinished. It was to show that removing material could create an ____6____ (REVERSE) change: once a layer was taken away, it could not simply be put back in its original state.

For this reason, recording was treated as a ____7____ (RESPONSIBLE) shared by the whole team. A sketch or photograph without a location label might look interesting while being difficult to interpret later. The visitors' guide acknowledged some remaining ____8____ (CERTAIN), explaining which features had been identified confidently and which still had more than one possible explanation.

questions.prompt: Gap 1 (ARCHAEOLOGY): Use an adjective. Use one word.
questions.explanation: 题面要求形容词，archaeological/archeological均可；archaeology是名词，archaeologist表示考古学家，均不符合所要求的形容词形式。

questions.prompt: Gap 2 (ERODE): Write the correct form. Use one word.
questions.explanation: vulnerable to后接名词erosion表示侵蚀。

questions.prompt: Gap 3 (ACCESS): Write the correct form. Use one word.
questions.explanation: be后用形容词accessible，表示可进入接近。

questions.prompt: Gap 4 (STEADY): Write the correct form. Use one word.
questions.explanation: 修饰changed用副词steadily。

questions.prompt: Gap 5 (COMPARE): Write the correct form. Use one word.
questions.explanation: a comparison between为名词搭配。

questions.prompt: Gap 6 (REVERSE): Write the negative adjective. Use one word.
questions.explanation: 下一句不能放回原状态，题面指定否定形容词irreversible；reversible意义相反。

questions.prompt: Gap 7 (RESPONSIBLE): Write the correct form. Use one word.
questions.explanation: a...shared by后用名词responsibility，表示共同责任。

questions.prompt: Gap 8 (CERTAIN): Write the negative noun. Use one word.
questions.explanation: some remaining uncertainty可用抽象单数，uncertainties可指多处未定解释，两者均合；题面要求否定名词，certainty和形容词uncertain不合。

units.title: 初二语法：音乐社乘火车的车票

materials.title: Keeping the Ticket
materials.text:
Our music club travelled to a nearby town by train last weekend. We had bought the tickets online, but our teacher asked us ____1____ (CHECK) the departure time again on Friday evening. One of the trains had been cancelled.

At the station, a member of staff showed ____2____ (WE) which platform to use. We did not simply follow the largest crowd, because people were travelling to several different places. I listened ____3____ (CAREFUL) to the announcement and compared it with our tickets.

There were enough seats for everybody, although we did not all sit together. My friend offered her place to a passenger ____4____ was carrying a sleeping baby. The passenger thanked her and put a small bag under the seat.

After about half an hour, we ____5____ (ARRIVE) at our stop. The town centre was ____6____ (CLOSE) than we had expected, so we walked instead of taking a bus. At the concert hall, we changed into our club shirts.

On the return journey, the teacher asked us to look after our own tickets. She would help ____7____ anyone had a problem, but she wanted us to try reading the information ____8____ (WE). I kept mine until I had left the station, then put it into the notebook where I recorded our trips.

questions.prompt: Gap 1 (CHECK) Use one to 2 words.
questions.explanation: ask somebody to do为不定式结构。

questions.prompt: Gap 2 (WE) Use one word.
questions.explanation: showed后作间接宾语，使用us。

questions.prompt: Gap 3 (CAREFUL) Use one word.
questions.explanation: 修饰listened用副词carefully。

questions.prompt: Gap 4: Write one suitable word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: passenger为人且关系词作主语，who/that均可，whose需后接名词。

questions.prompt: Gap 5 (ARRIVE) Use one to 2 words.
questions.explanation: 过去叙事中可用arrived，突出已完成到达也可用had arrived；都在两词边界内，arrive/arriving不构成这里独立谓语。

questions.prompt: Gap 6 (CLOSE) Use one word.
questions.explanation: than要求比较级closer。

questions.prompt: Gap 7: Write one suitable word. Use one word.
questions.explanation: 老师表示遇到问题愿帮助，条件if、时间when和每逢whenever均能成立；unless把帮助条件反转。

questions.prompt: Gap 8 (WE) Use one word.
questions.explanation: read the information ourselves表示我们自己阅读，用反身代词强调。

units.title: 初三阅读：橱窗倒影里的那个人

materials.title: Before the Photo Went on the Wall
materials.text:
For a class exhibition called “Our Daily Journeys”, Jia photographed the streets between her home and school. Her teacher had set a clear class rule: if a person could be recognised in a photograph, the photographer needed that person's permission before displaying it.

Jia's favourite picture showed a bakery window full of bread. She thought it contained no people. When she enlarged it on the classroom screen, however, a classmate noticed the baker's face reflected in the glass. Jia had been looking at the loaves, so she had missed the reflection.

She visited the bakery and showed the picture to its owner. He liked the photograph but did not want his face in the school exhibition. Jia was disappointed. She asked whether she could remove the reflection by cropping the picture. The owner said he was happy for the bread display alone to be shown.

The cropped picture met the permission rule, but it no longer showed the doorway that had connected the bakery to Jia's daily route. She decided to use a different photograph: the empty pavement outside just before the shop opened. The owner agreed that no identifiable person appeared in it.

At the exhibition, Jia placed a short caption beneath the new image explaining why this shop mattered on her walk to school. She did not display the rejected picture as an example, because doing so would have created the same problem again. The experience taught her to check the whole image, including its edges and reflections, before deciding who was or was not in it.

questions.prompt: What did the class rule require?
options: Permission before showing a photograph containing a recognisable person.
Permission from every shop in the town before walking to school.
A photograph of a person in every exhibition entry.
A ban on taking any pictures of buildings.
questions.explanation: A正确：班规针对展示可辨认人物照片需取得本人许可。B不是行走许可；C没有每张必须有人；D不禁止拍建筑。

questions.prompt: Why had Jia initially overlooked the baker?
options: He was hidden behind a classmate in the classroom.
She was concentrating on the bread rather than the reflection.
He appeared only after she changed the image digitally.
The class rule excluded all reflected faces.
questions.explanation: B正确：她一直看面包，未注意玻璃倒影，放大后同学发现。A人物不在教室里躲藏；C原图已有倒影；D可辨人像包括倒影，未获豁免。

questions.prompt: What did the baker permit?
options: Displaying his face if his name was removed.
Using the rejected photo as an example on the wall.
Showing the bread display without his reflected face.
Showing his face only beside another bakery.
questions.explanation: C正确：店主同意只展示面包陈列，拒绝露脸。A没说去名字可露脸；B未同意拒绝图片示例；D没有异店条件。

questions.prompt: Why did Jia choose another photograph instead of the cropped one?
options: The cropped image was too large for the classroom screen.
The baker had forbidden every possible view of the shop.
The teacher had required a different camera.
Cropping had removed the doorway relevant to her daily journey.
questions.explanation: D正确：裁剪删除了与每日路线有联系的店门，所以另选开门前空人行道。A不是尺寸问题；B店主允许面包展示；C没有换相机要求。

questions.prompt: What did Jia avoid doing at the exhibition?
options: Displaying the rejected image to explain the problem.
Writing a caption about the shop’s connection with her route.
Using a picture without any identifiable person.
Checking whether reflections contained people.
questions.explanation: A正确：她不把被拒图当示例，因为仍会展示未授权人像。B她写了说明；C她采用无人可辨图；D正是学到要检查倒影。

units.title: 高一专项：整理老照片与街边旧面包炉

materials.title: Reading a Family Photo Box
materials.text:
A box of family photographs can contain more questions than answers. Begin by keeping each picture together with any envelope or note already beside it. Before cleaning a surface, look for pencil marks on the back and edges. ____1____ Work on one small group at a time so that these connections do not get lost.

Do not wait until every face has a name before recording what you know. ____2____ For example, a year written on an original envelope can help to organise several otherwise unidentified pictures. Make clear where the information came from.

If someone thinks that a figure might be a particular cousin, write down who suggested the identification and why. ____3____ Another relative may later provide a different explanation, and it helps to know which parts were observations and which were guesses.

When recording a spoken memory, keep the speaker's words but also ask about sequence. ____4____ A person may begin with the funniest incident and then return to the journey that came before it. Your notes can preserve the telling while making the timeline easier to follow.

Finally, photograph or scan a picture before sharing it widely. ____5____ Passing around a copy reduces the need to send the only original from house to house. The aim is to make the family's knowledge more accessible while retaining the small clues that future relatives may need.

questions.prompt: Gap 1: Choose one sentence from the seven shared candidates.
options: You can make another copy if a relative wants one.
These details may be part of the photograph's history rather than dirt to be removed.
Guessing confidently is always better than leaving a name unknown.
A date that you know is useful even if you cannot identify everyone in the picture.
The order in which people remember a story may be different from the order in which events happened.
Every photograph with a faded corner should be thrown away.
A separate note lets you record a possibility without making it look certain.

materials.title: The Oven in the Old Street
materials.text:
Our town's old bread oven had been closed for several years. Last spring, a local group ____1____ (INVITE) a baker to examine it. After repairs were completed, the oven ____2____ (OPEN) for a small demonstration.

I went with my grandmother, ____3____ remembered taking dough there as a child. She described how families had once used their own marks to recognise ____4____ (THEY) loaves. The baker showed us a few simple tools but did not ask visitors to operate the oven.

While we ____5____ (WAIT), my grandmother told me about the smell in the street on baking days. I had walked past the building many times without ____6____ (KNOW) what it had once been used for.

The demonstration ended with bread already prepared by the baker. It was divided ____7____ small pieces so that everyone could taste it. The group hoped ____8____ (HOLD) another event later in the summer, but first it wanted to hear what visitors had found useful.

At home, my grandmother drew a picture of the mark her family had used. I wrote the date beside it. The drawing was not a perfect copy of the old mark, but it helped me ask more ____9____ (INTEREST) questions. I kept it with a short account of the day rather ____10____ putting it in the drawer with unrelated papers.

questions.prompt: Gap 1 (INVITE) Use one word.
questions.explanation: Last spring表过去，invited。

questions.explanation: 此题要求过去被动，维修完成后烤炉向参观者开放，was opened。

questions.explanation: loaves前用形容词性物主代词their。

questions.explanation: without后动名词knowing。

questions.explanation: divide into pieces固定搭配，onto表示到表面不合分份。

questions.explanation: hope to do用不定式to hold。

questions.explanation: 题面指定令人感兴趣，使用interesting；interested可在其他语境描述显露兴趣，但不是本题指定的引起兴趣含义。

questions.explanation: rather than作选择对比，then为时间词。

units.title: 高二专项：安静的桌游伙伴与渡轮候船室

materials.title: Making Space at the Game Table
materials.text:
When one player is quiet during a group game, do not assume at once that they are lost or uninterested. ____1____ That silent attention can itself be a form of participation. Watch whether the player is following the turns before deciding that an explanation is needed.

If you want to involve the player in a decision, make the question manageable. Asking whether they would prefer the blue cards or the red cards gives them a clear starting point. ____2____ Once the person has made a choice, allow it to matter rather than immediately replacing it with your own.

You may also want to invite someone to explain a move they have made. ____3____ Ask first whether they would like to share their thinking. Calling on them without warning can turn a friendly game into a performance they did not choose.

If a person declines, avoid repeating the request in front of everybody. ____4____ Away from the pressure of the table, you may learn that they would prefer a smaller group or simply need more time.

None of these steps guarantees that a quiet person will become talkative. ____5____ A well-hosted game can include different ways of taking part, provided that people have genuine opportunities to choose and are not treated as less capable merely because they speak less.

materials.title: Two Lines at the Ferry Terminal
materials.text:
Last summer, my cousin and I ____1____ (ARRIVE) at the ferry terminal earlier than necessary. We had expected to queue outside, but the new waiting room had already opened. It was in a building ____2____ had once been used for storing fishing equipment.

The entrance was ____3____ (FAR) from the bus stop than the old one. Instead of ____4____ (HURRY) across the yard, we followed the painted signs along a marked path. A member of staff showed ____5____ (WE) where to wait.

Passengers travelling on foot stood in one line, while bicycles ____6____ (KEEP) in a separate area. The arrangement left enough space for people carrying large bags. The staff asked everyone ____7____ (HAVE) their tickets ready before approaching the gate.

At first, I did not understand the ____8____ (DIFFERENT) between the two coloured signs above the doors. After ____9____ (READ) the explanation beside the timetable, I saw that one door was for people arriving and the other for people departing.

Knowing which flow to follow made the room feel less confusing. The signs did not tell us every detail of the journey, but they showed ____10____ we needed to do next. When boarding began, we joined the correct line without asking the staff to repeat the whole explanation.

questions.explanation: the difference between为名词搭配。

questions.explanation: after作介词后动名词reading，此题明确要求-ing形式。

questions.explanation: what可引名词性从句；all/everything后也可接省略that的限定从句，三种写法都表达下一步所需做的事。that不能单独同时补足do的宾语；which在此没有明确可作do宾语的动作选集。

materials.title: A Manageable Memory Question
materials.text:
A small class project can teach useful lessons about memory, provided that its question is narrow. Before comparing two learning methods, decide what you will count as remembering. ____1____ “The learner seemed confident” is less precise than a count of words recalled correctly after a stated interval.

Think about the order of the tasks. If everyone tries one method first and the other second, the second attempt may benefit from familiarity with the test. ____2____ One possible design is to vary the order across participants, while keeping the materials as comparable as you can.

Try the instructions with a few people before running the main activity. ____3____ Perhaps a timing rule is unclear or a response sheet has too little space. Repairing such problems early is different from changing the procedure merely because you dislike the result.

Even a well-run class project will have limits. Its volunteers may share an age, a language background or a particular interest in learning. ____4____ A result for those people is not automatically a result for every kind of learner.

Finally, keep the original records and describe how they were collected. ____5____ An unexpected pattern can be more informative than the one you hoped to see, particularly if you have preserved enough detail to consider another explanation.

questions.prompt: Gap 1: Choose one sentence from the seven shared candidates.
options: You should change the test whenever the first results look disappointing.

Define the result in a way that another person could record too.
A large total automatically removes every possible source of bias.
The aim is to find out what happened, not to make one condition win.
Otherwise, an apparent improvement might simply reflect extra practice.
That limit should appear in the conclusion, not disappear from it.

materials.title: The Notes beside the Printed Page
materials.text:
Hardly ____1____ (WE/ARRIVE) at the old library when the guide asked us to examine a book whose margins were full of notes. I had expected a clean printed page, not a conversation between readers from different periods.

Some notes ____2____ (WRITE) in a much darker ink than others. A librarian had already recorded the places ____3____ each kind of ink appeared. She did not assume that every change of colour meant a different person.

The most interesting note was a question ____4____ (ADD) beside an account of a journey. Another reader had answered it several pages later, ____5____ (REFER) back to the earlier page number. The two entries made sense only when they were read together.

The guide asked us ____6____ the printed author and the note-writers agreed. There was no simple yes-or-no answer. At one point, a reader praised a description; at another, the same hand seemed ____7____ (DOUBT) about a date.

To avoid damaging the volume, we used copies for the detailed work. Each copy included the page edge so that no small mark would be lost ____8____ it. Looking at the margins changed my ____9____ (UNDERSTAND) of the book. It had not passed through time untouched. ____10____ had survived was a printed text together with traces of the ways people had used it.
